teaser_de: Was wird aus den YAC Bros, dem Receiver-Duo der 49ers?
title_en: The end of the YAC Bros?
teaser_en: What becomes of the YAC Bros, the 49ers’ receiver duo?
body_en:
NFL insider Ian Rapoport was the first to report today that the San Francisco 49ers will try to trade Deebo Samuel this offseason. Shortly afterwards, ESPN reported that Samuel himself had already asked Kyle Shanahan for a trade during the exit meetings after the last game of the season. In his own words, he now had to do what was best for himself personally. He was more than grateful for the opportunity he had received with the 49ers, but now it was time for them to find a new team for him. So the YAC Bros (YAC = yards after catch) around Deebo Samuel, Brandon Aiyuk and George Kittle seem to be coming to an end soon.

These statements contradict those of general manager John Lynch. After the exit meetings, Matt Maiocco of NBC Sports Bay Area had asked him whether he expected Deebo Samuel back for the coming season. Lynch replied that the 49ers had no intention of letting good, deserving players go. These developments show once again that statements at offseason press conferences should never be taken 100 percent at face value, and that our front office, too, likes to play games with the public on contract matters.

## So what exactly does this mean for Deebo Samuel?

If we think back exactly three years, history is repeating itself. Back then, too, Deebo Samuel asked for a trade. The end result was an early extension of his rookie contract. He signed for three more years at $71.5 million, $58.1 million of it guaranteed. He would now be entering the final year of that contract.

Deebo Samuel's contract is complicated because it has already been restructured several times, which means some bonuses have not yet counted against the salary cap. Essentially, the restructures kept pushing his cap hits further back.

If Deebo Samuel is traded or cut, exactly these amounts have to be charged as so-called dead cap. Deebo's salary for the coming season is particularly delicate: most of it only becomes due as a bonus on March 22, 2025. This bonus counts one fifth in 2025 and the rest in 2026.

If Deebo stays on the team, he will carry a cap hit of $15 million in the 2025 season. After his contract ends, however, around $32 million in dead cap will still remain, so we will have a cap hit for Deebo Samuel in the coming years as well, without him playing for us. In contract language, these are referred to as void years.

If Deebo is traded or cut before March 22, 2025, about $31 million in dead cap stays on the books for 2025. At this point, the NFL also allows a so-called post-June 1 designation. For players who are cut (not traded) after June 1, the dead cap may be spread over two years. The designation allows a team to cut up to two players before June 1 but still treat them like a cut after June 1. So the 49ers could at least split the $31 million in dead cap over two years (2025 and 2026).

You can take a closer look at Deebo Samuel's contract here, for example:

[https://overthecap.com/player/deebo-samuel/7827](https://overthecap.com/player/deebo-samuel/7827)

## So what now?

The 49ers front office now has to weigh whether or not they want Deebo Samuel on the roster for $15 million, since the dead cap won't change much in the other scenarios.

For a trade, they would need to find a team willing to take on Samuel for the final year of his contract. In cap terms, that would be around $16 million in cap hits spread over two years. Deebo Samuel is probably interesting for teams currently playing with a young quarterback, since Deebo can be used both as a returner and as a matchup weapon.
